summary: Vallejo sits on the northern shore of San Pablo Bay, and its geography delivers something genuinely rare in the Bay Area: waterfront hillside terrain with unobstructed views across the strait toward Marin County, at a median home price of $557,500 — roughly half what comparable bay-facing cities to the south command. The city sprawls across 48 square miles of rolling hills, which means the urban fabric is uneven: a compact, walkable downtown along the waterfront gives way to car-dependent residential stretches separated by elevation changes and freeway corridors, making the city feel more like a collection of distinct pockets than a single cohesive grid. The former Mare Island Naval Shipyard, once one of the largest military installations on the West Coast, left behind a vast peninsula of repurposed industrial land that continues to shape the local economy alongside healthcare (Kaiser Permanente and Sutter Health operate major facilities here) and the nearby Six Flags Discovery Kingdom. With a median household income of $89,496, the home-price-to-income ratio lands around 6.2 — stretched but meaningfully less punishing than most of the Bay Area — though a motor vehicle theft rate of nearly 900 per 100,000 and a violent crime rate above 800 per 100,000 are numbers worth sitting with. Annual highs averaging 70°F with nearly nine hours of daily sunshine make for mild, fog-free conditions compared to San Francisco just 30 miles south. Vallejo is essentially a Bay Area city that traded proximity and polish for space and affordability, and the commute — whether by ferry to the Financial District or by car on I-80 — is the daily price of that bargain.
